blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A River circuit may only be worked from week 8 to week 23. How does the lesson's model state that?

options.text: As a fixed interval in each crew's NoOverlap list
options.says: Fixed intervals in NoOverlap state a crew's time off, not a circuit's window.

options.text: As the domain of each start variable of the circuit
options.says: Right: the start's domain is the union of the starts that fit a window.

options.text: As one Boolean per window, with two enforced rows
options.says: That alternative was rejected: more variables to say what a domain says.

options.text: As a must row that forces the trim into those weeks
options.says: A must is t = 1 and says nothing about weeks.

origin.section: Each Calendar Is a Constraint Kind CP-SAT Already Has

questions.stem: The steps/04 plan carried $3,989k and was not proven optimal; the calendar plan carries $4,571k. Why may the lesson still say the calendars cost at least $582k?

options.text: Both plans were proven optimal under the same solver settings
options.says: The steps/04 plan was FEASIBLE, not proven optimal.

options.text: The calendars took $582k out of the season's trimming budget
options.says: The budget is $962k in both runs; the $582k is risk.

options.text: The calendar plan trims more circuits than the steps/04 plan
options.says: The calendar plan trims eight circuits, one fewer than before.

options.text: The $3,989k plan is real, so the best without them is no worse
options.says: Right: a real plan of the model bounds its best, so the best without calendars carries at most $3,989k.

origin.section: Every Calendar Kept, at a Price

questions.stem: A test says a 3-week trim with windows at weeks 0-1 and 5-7 must start at week 5. Why is week 5 the one right answer?

options.text: Risk grows each week, so the earliest allowed start is best
options.says: Right: since risk grows, the earliest allowed week is the rule's answer.

options.text: The trim may run through weeks 2 to 4 at a slower pace
options.says: A trim cannot run through the closed weeks 2 to 4.

options.text: Weeks 0 and 1 are held for the crew's time off that season
options.says: The test gives the crew no time off; weeks 0-1 are too short for 3 weeks.

options.text: A later start carries the same risk, so week 6 fits too
options.says: Risk grows, so the earliest allowed week is best and the test asks for it.
